title: FancyZones "quick layout switch" ignores remappings in Keyboard Manager

judgment.rationale: The report gives an exact interoperability test: remap CapsLock to Ctrl, configure a FancyZones quick-layout shortcut using Ctrl+Win+Alt+number, then compare physical Ctrl with CapsLock. The code uses a registered global hotkey while Keyboard Manager synthesizes remapped input; their interaction is plausible but unconfirmed.
evidence: The issue title identifies FancyZones quick-layout switching as ignoring Keyboard Manager remaps.
The described sequence compares a physical Ctrl chord with the remapped CapsLock-as-Ctrl chord.
FancyZones registers quick-layout hotkeys with RegisterHotKey; Keyboard Manager handles remapping through its low-level keyboard path.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the physical-versus-remapped modifier comparison and trace hotkey registration/input delivery before changing either module.

fix_assessment.rationale: A registered FancyZones hotkey may not recognize the synthetic modifier event produced by Keyboard Manager, but the issue has not been reproduced on a current build and the interaction is not established.

proposed_fixes.title: Make FancyZones quick-layout hotkeys recognize Keyboard Manager remapped modifiers
proposed_fixes.root_cause: FancyZones' RegisterHotKey path may observe the remapped CapsLock-to-Ctrl chord differently from a physical Ctrl chord, causing the registered Ctrl+Win+Alt+number shortcut not to activate.
plan: Reproduce with only CapsLock-to-Ctrl enabled and one FancyZones quick-layout chord; compare physical Ctrl+Win+Alt+number against CapsLock+Win+Alt+number.
Trace the low-level key event and registered-hotkey delivery for each chord to determine whether the remapped modifier is injected, filtered, or not reflected in the registered combination.
If the mismatch is confirmed, implement the smallest compatible integration between Keyboard Manager remapped state and FancyZones hotkey handling, preserving ordinary RegisterHotKey behavior.
Add a regression test covering physical and remapped Ctrl activation for the same FancyZones layout.
verification: The quick-layout action fires with both physical Ctrl and CapsLock-remapped Ctrl.
Unrelated Ctrl shortcuts and existing FancyZones hotkeys retain their behavior.
Disabling the remap restores the baseline physical-key behavior without duplicate layout activation.

confidence.rationale: The two module paths provide a concrete integration hypothesis, but the event delivery behavior has not been traced and may be subject to Windows hotkey semantics.

issue_context.summary: A FancyZones quick-layout hotkey apparently does not activate when its Ctrl modifier is produced by Keyboard Manager's CapsLock-to-Ctrl remap.
known_information: The issue is labeled Issue-Bug, Product-FancyZones, Needs-Triage, and Product-Keyboard Manager.
The reported quick-layout chord uses Ctrl+Win+Alt+number.
The comparison is between physical Ctrl and CapsLock remapped to Ctrl.
FancyZones registers quick-layout shortcuts through RegisterHotKey, while Keyboard Manager uses low-level keyboard remapping.
inferences: The registered hotkey may not treat remapped/synthetic Ctrl the same as physical Ctrl, but no event trace confirms this.
The report could also depend on hotkey registration timing or a conflicting system shortcut.
issue_context.analysis: This is a focused cross-module interoperability case, not an established defect in either module independently. The required evidence is the physical-versus-remapped comparison plus a trace of whether the registered hotkey fires.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body; there are no comments or attachments.
Read FancyZones.cpp quick-layout RegisterHotKey registration and Keyboard Manager's remapping/event path; the connection is plausible but not confirmed.

actions.label: Design the FancyZones remapped-hotkey integration
actions.note: The design must remain conditional on reproducing the physical-versus-remapped mismatch and tracing hotkey delivery.

actions.label: Compare physical and remapped Ctrl in FancyZones

reproduce.title: Test quick-layout activation with a remapped Ctrl key
prerequisites: A clean Keyboard Manager configuration with CapsLock mapped to Ctrl.
One FancyZones quick-layout shortcut configured as Ctrl+Win+Alt+number.
steps: Press the configured chord using physical Ctrl and confirm whether the selected quick layout activates.
Repeat with CapsLock in place of Ctrl while keeping Win, Alt, and the number identical.
Disable the CapsLock-to-Ctrl mapping and repeat to establish the baseline.
If only the remapped chord fails, trace whether the matching registered hotkey fires and whether the low-level event is marked synthetic.
reproduce.expected_result: Both physical and remapped Ctrl activate the same layout, or the trace identifies where the remapped chord stops reaching FancyZones.
